title: Small object factorizations for a set in a locally presentable category
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with Hom sets in a fixed universe $\mathcal U$ and all $\mathcal U$-small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose $\mathcal C$ is locally presentable: for some infinite regular $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, a $\mathcal U$-small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve $\kappa$-filtered colimits generates every object under such colimits; $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram of fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ still has cardinality less than $\kappa$. Let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set of morphisms of $\mathcal C$. Write $R=I^{\square}$ for the morphisms admitting a diagonal filler in every commutative square with left side in $I$, and $L={}^{\square}R$ for those admitting a filler against every right side in $R$. There is a functorial factorization $f=p_f i_f$ of every morphism, with $i_f\in L$ and $p_f\in R$. Functorial means every commutative square $(a,b):f\to g$ induces a map $m(a,b)$ of middle objects satisfying $m(a,b)i_f=i_g a$ and $p_gm(a,b)=bp_f$, preserving identities and composition.

proof.text: For each $i:A_i\to B_i$ in $I$, apply [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] to $A_i$ in the given locally presentable category. Choose an infinite regular $\tau_i\in\mathcal U$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,-)$ preserves all $\mathcal U$-small $\tau_i$-filtered colimits. The ranks may vary with $i$; no single rank is asserted at this point.

source.place: Agent proof, step 1: objectwise presentability, Mathlib Presentable/LocallyPresentable.lean:93-101.

proof.text: For each $i\in I$ take the set $T_i$ of ordinals below the initial ordinal of cardinality $\tau_i$; its cardinality is $\tau_i$ and it belongs to $\mathcal U$. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the coproduct $T=\coprod_{i\in I}T_i$ indexed by the given small set $I$. Obtain an infinite regular $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ with $|T|<\lambda$. For each $i$, the map $x\mapsto(i,x)$ injects $T_i$ into $T$, hence $\tau_i=|T_i|\leq |T|<\lambda$. The same application works when $I$ is empty, because then $T$ is empty.

source.place: Agent proof, step 2: common bound from Mathlib SetTheory/Cardinal/HasCardinalLT.lean:201-206 applied to the disjoint union; the injection of each fibre is explicit.

proof.text: The ordinal category $\lambda$ is $\tau_i$-filtered for each $i$. Indeed, a diagram with fewer than $\tau_i$ morphisms has fewer than $\tau_i$ objects, since each object contributes its identity. Its object images are ordinals $\alpha<\lambda$. Each such ordinal has cardinality less than $\lambda$; their union has cardinality less than $\lambda$ by regularity, since there are fewer than $\tau_i<\lambda$ of them. Their supremum is therefore an ordinal $\beta<\lambda$ and is an upper bound, so the unique arrows to $\beta$ form the desired cocone. For the empty diagram choose $0<\lambda$. By the preservation property obtained in step 1, $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,-)$ preserves the colimit of every $\lambda$-indexed diagram. Thus this holds for every generating domain.

source.place: Agent proof, step 3: regular-union argument and the definition of filteredness and presentability.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cardinal-small-object-factorization] using the regular cardinal $\lambda$ and the preservation established in step 3. Its Hom-smallness, smallness of $I$, and existence of all small colimits are exactly hypotheses of this item. All ordinal index categories used here are $\mathcal U$-small because $\lambda\in\mathcal U$; coproducts over lifting squares are also small, since for fixed $i$ the pairs of maps are a subset of $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,X)\times\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,Y)$, and $I$ is small. Obtain $Z$, $i_f$ and $p_f$ with $p_f i_f=f$, $i_f\in L$ and $p_f\in R$.

For a commutative square $(a,b):f\to g$, put $m(a,b)=Z(a,b)$. The two naturality equations in [lem-coef-cardinal-small-object-factorization] give $m(a,b)i_f=i_g a$ and $p_g m(a,b)=b p_f$. The identity and composition laws of its functor $Z$ give the required laws for $m$. This is precisely the functoriality in the item.
